headline: Would You CHASE 🏃‍♂️ a Friend For £5 💵??
text:
BROKE 🪙 vibes everywhere 🌍 as New Yorkers 🗽 spill the TEA ☕ on the TINIEST 💸 amounts they'd actually CHASE 🏃 a friend for after picking 🍽️ up dinner bills 🧾 or taxi rides 🚕 with that casual promise 🤝 they'll pay you back later but days drag on 🕰️ and the cash 💵 never shows up 😤!! At what POINT 📍 do you hit them with the awkward reminder 📲 and how SMALL 🐜 is too SMALL 🐜 to bother chasing without looking like a CHEAPSKATE 🪙?? For some $5 💵 or roughly £3.70 is totally worth a gentle nudge 🫳 while for others anything under $20 💰 feels way more CRINGE 😬 than just eating the loss 🍽️ and moving on with your life 🏃‍♂️!!

Henry Payne 🧔 straight up admits he's sent a request for $8.50 💸 but draws the hard LINE 🛑 at anything lower than $8 and says he'd chase someone ONCE 🔂 but two requests is straight up INSANE 🤪!! The 21-year-old New Yorker 🗽 adds he'd rather SWALLOW 😋 that $8.50 loss than fire off another desperate ping 📨 and he even owns up to being the forgetful one himself sometimes saying for everyone he hasn't repaid feel free to DOUBLE 📨 request him without hesitation bro 🫡!! Nouria 👩‍🎓 and her buddy Kaz 👨‍🎓 both students in New York agree that money 💰 talks with friends can get SUPER AWKWARD 😣 especially when you're both BROKE AF 🪙 and every extra dollar literally COUNTS 📊!!

Kaz Jahanbini at 19 years old says needing to even ASK 🙋 for payback in the first place is already frustrating as hell because if someone bought him something he'd immediately VENMO 💸 them back so he's always wondering what's the HOLDUP ⏳ with them?? His golden RULE 📜 for juggling friendship 👥 and finances is to keep your WALLET 👛 close but your friends even CLOSER 🤗 and his pal Nouria nods along saying as a fellow student every extra dollar counts but she'd usually only chase a friend if it was more than $10 💵 or so!! A fresh STUDY 📊 reveals that a whopping 76% of Gen Z who fronted cash for group trips 🧳 or events say they never got fully repaid and 55% admit it created real tension or straight up damaged the relationship 💔 which hits different when you're all BROKE 🪙 together!!

British student Betsie Brooke-Taylor at 19 swears her threshold is a fiver 💷 because every little HELPS 🛠️ and she spots a clear cultural GAP 🌍 between Brits and Americans even though we're all broke she thinks Americans are a bit more GENEROUS 🫳 with small debts!! Betsie also credits technology 📱 for making tiny repayments way easier stateside where apps like Venmo are everywhere with over 95 million accounts letting you send polite reminders 🛎️ if someone ghosts your request but in the UK you gotta hunt for account numbers and sort codes which nobody has handy anyway 😩!! Meanwhile Annika Violet feels totally different about confronting friends who owe her and says the amount depends on whether she's been consistently paying for them like if it's always her card then yeah she'll request that $5 💸 without blinking!!

Annika claims she's so CONFRONTATIONAL 🗣️ that money talks don't faze her at all and if you're truly her friend you'd just PAY 🏧 her back immediately but her friend Hanako Stepper finds it awkward as hell and admits she's never actually chased anyone instead just feeling SAD 😢 if the money never comes!! Annika's sage advice to the shy ones is to be brave and BOLD 💪 and if they give you flak about a small request maybe it's a red flag they're not a good friend after all 🚩!! Money expert Laura Pomfret confirms loads of people especially Brits feel embarrassed asking for payback because we're so British about it and scared of being labeled a cheapskate 🪙 but her top tips include just asking politely without overthinking and never convincing yourself the debt is too tiny to mention because if you want it back the amount literally shouldn't matter at all!!

Ella Feuille and her friend Katrina both 21 and 19 respectively say the amount itself starts to matter less when the same friend repeatedly fails to pay you back like Ella draws her line around $15 💵 and might ask up to three times before giving up but she won't forget and now makes sure those flaky friends put big stuff on their own card instead!! Katrina prefers the smoother method where nobody pays each other back they just take turns buying things 🍔 which keeps the friendship drama-free and way less awkward overall!! Several folks the BBC chatted with echoed that repeated deadbeats change the whole game and you should remember it next time you're about to whip out your wallet again 🪪 because at the end of the day we're all broke but some friendships are worth more than a fiver anyway right??
